sources.section: Build your own Emulator / Virtual Machine

summary.title: Write your Own Virtual Machine
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a working LC-3 virtual machine in C by simulating its memory, registers, condition flags, and fetch-decode-execute loop, then implementing instructions like ADD and LDI.
keywords: build a virtual machine in c
takeaways: A VM is a program that simulates a CPU and memory, executing machine code via a fetch-increment-decode-execute loop.
The LC-3 has 65,536 16-bit memory locations, 8 general purpose registers, a program counter, and a condition flags register.
Instructions are 16 bits with a 4-bit opcode; ADD supports register and immediate modes, and immediate values must be sign-extended.
Condition flags (positive, zero, negative) must be updated whenever a register is written.
The full VM is about 250 lines of C, and the tutorial covers loading programs, trap routines, and platform specifics.
summary.summary: This is a literate programming tutorial by Justin Meiners and Ryan Pendleton that walks through writing a virtual machine in C for the LC-3 educational architecture. It explains the purpose of VMs compared with emulators, compilers, the JVM, and Ethereum, then sets up memory, registers, opcodes, and condition flags. It shows an assembly example, outlines the main fetch-decode-execute loop, and implements ADD and LDI step by step, with the remaining instructions, trap routines, and image loading deferred to later sections. The final code is said to be about 250 lines of C.
